rpo_rto.target_rto: 4 hours for manual restore or failover after restore drills pass

current_supabase_usage.postgrest_data_api: app uses @supabase/supabase-js with anon and service-role keys; self-hosted PostgreSQL alone is not API-compatible
current_supabase_usage.rls_and_grants: migrations and regression tests depend on anon/authenticated/service_role grants and RLS behavior
current_supabase_usage.auth: admin authentication uses NextAuth Google with JWT sessions; Supabase Auth is present in local config but no production app dependency was identified
current_supabase_usage.storage: Supabase storage is enabled in local config, but no app storage client usage was identified
current_supabase_usage.realtime: Supabase realtime is enabled in local config and CSP permits wss://*.supabase.co, but no app realtime client usage was identified
current_supabase_usage.edge_functions: no app dependency on Supabase Edge Functions was identified
current_supabase_usage.search: public search uses Postgres full-text search through public.search_articles
current_supabase_usage.backups: current app backup helper is a limited REST export and not a full database backup

target_topology.standby: optional async standby only after PITR and restore drills are proven; no multi-writer topology
target_topology.pooling: pgBouncer required if Vercel/app connection count or direct Postgres access exceeds safe limits
target_topology.data_api: choose PostgREST-compatible layer or app rewrite before cutover; do not point supabase-js at bare Postgres
target_topology.network: database and management dashboard must be private or behind a reviewed access boundary; no public database port
target_topology.dashboard: read-only/admin dashboard requires separate access-control review before exposure

feature_mapping.Supabase Postgres tables/functions: self-hosted PostgreSQL migrations and restore validation
feature_mapping.Supabase REST/PostgREST API: deploy compatible PostgREST layer or rewrite app to server-owned database APIs
feature_mapping.anon and service_role keys: replace with explicit JWT/RLS model or app server credentials in protected secrets
feature_mapping.RLS/grants: port policies and run local RLS regressions against restored non-production data
feature_mapping.Supabase Auth: keep NextAuth for admin unless a future app issue proves Supabase Auth is used
feature_mapping.Supabase Storage: keep explicitly not used; choose R2/S3/local storage only if app usage appears
feature_mapping.Supabase Realtime: keep explicitly not used unless a future feature requires websocket replication
feature_mapping.full-text search: keep Postgres full-text search and GIN indexes
feature_mapping.backups: replace limited REST export with encrypted full database backups plus WAL/PITR

implementation_plan.required_evidence: production Supabase project ref, schema dump, row counts, extensions, grants, RLS policies, API keys inventory, storage/realtime/auth usage confirmation
restore latest production-like dump to isolated Postgres and run restore_validation.sql plus app regression tests
PostgREST-compatible API or app rewrite validated against staging env vars and RLS/contract tests
encrypted off-box base backups, WAL archiving, PITR restore drill, backup freshness alerts, and restore report
app can run against restored data in read-only staging with production writes still on Supabase
separate explicit approval, paused writers, final backup, final restore or replication catch-up, env switch, smoke tests, rollback window

rollback.before_cutover: discard the self-hosted target and keep Supabase
rollback.during_cutover: switch app and worker environment variables back to Supabase, resume writers only after consistency is confirmed
rollback.after_cutover: rollback only within the documented rollback window unless reverse replication is proven; otherwise run a forward recovery plan

blockers_for_deploy: production Supabase credentials and project metadata are not available in this backend repo
no full production dump, WAL archive, PITR restore drill, or non-production rehearsal evidence exists here
the app currently uses Supabase/PostgREST-style APIs, so a bare PostgreSQL server is not a drop-in replacement
protected backend apply and dashboard access boundaries are not yet approved for a database deployment
